answer_1.quote: Multimodal summarization with multimodal output (MSMO) has garnered more and more attention from researchers. Unlike unimodal output (e.g., text-only summary), MSMO aims at extracting the most salient information from different modalities and generating multimodal summaries, with a text summary and the most relevant images.
answer_1.outputs: The paper generates multimodal summaries consisting of a text summary and selected relevant images.

answer_2.quote: We propose mLLM-EVAL, an MSMO metric utilize the emergent abilities of multimodal LLMs that shows a high correlation with human judgments.

answer_3.quote: We propose mLLM-EVAL using multimodal LLMs for reference-free MSMO evaluation.
methods: attribute-specific prompts with chain-of-thoughts and scoring form

answer_4.quote: After having 1,562 multimodal summarization examples, we ask three annotators to evaluate the quality of the multimodal summaries.
answer_4.guideline: The annotators evaluate the following aspects: • Text Summary-Relevance: how well the summary captures the most relevant and salient information... • Text Summary-Coherence: how well the summary is organized with sentences logically connected... • Text Summary-Consistency: how factual and faithful the summary is to the source document... • Text Summary-Fluency: how fluent each sentence in the summary... • Summary Images: how well the selected summary images represent the content... • Text Summary-Summary Images Relevance: how well the summary text and summary images match... • Overall Quality: the overall quality of the generated multimodal summary.
